The resulting framework provides researchers with a map for benchmarking, comparing methods, and identifying knowledge gaps across machine learning disciplines, such as supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and generative modeling. The authors open-source this framework for the research community to use, with potential applications in guiding related work sections and highlighting paper contributions.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution within catalytic fixed bed reactors is critical for both optimal production yield and operational stability.  However, obtaining precise temperature readings simultaneously with good spatial and temporal resolution in these systems remains difficult. Our research utilizes the capabilities of real-time MRI imaging in conjunction with the temperature-dependent shift in water's proton resonance frequency to obtain in situ temperature measurements in a cylindrical fixed bed reactor. The temperature distribution was monitored as the reactor was heated from room temperature to 60°C using hot gas and subsequently as a localized cool gas was introduced via a rotating distribution plate. The results show the existence of temperature uniformity issues even when the reactor is steadily heated, and provide insights into the complex interplay between gas density and magnetic susceptibility that affects MRI-based temperature imaging. The temperature data obtained through MRI was verified against independent temperature readings obtained through fiber optic sensing, revealing a maximum margin of error of 2°C over a 2 to 58°C range. The findings highlight the potential of MRI as a valuable research tool for gaining in-depth, in situ understanding of temperature distribution and complex multiphase transport phenomena in fixed bed reactors.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic type of map functions that adhere to the b-principle, and is nearly equivalent to the set of oriented submersions in 2 dimensions. It demonstrates that the Madsen-Weiss theorem, which can be viewed as a variation of the standard Mumford Conjecture, is derivable from a specific application of the b-principle to oriented colored broken submersions, combined with the findings from Harer's stability theorem and Miller and Morita's work.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems on various types of finite element grids. By modeling the mechanical properties of heart muscle tissue using three-dimensional finite elasticity equations, researchers have transformed the problem into a nonlinear algebraic system. A combination of Newton-Krylov and BDDC/AMG solvers is employed to solve this large system. A comprehensive examination of the performance of the BDDC algorithm is also conducted. Ultimately, the study compares these algorithms for solving cardiac mechanics problems at both diastolic and systolic phases of the cardiac cycle.

The standard scaled Wigner matrix and its corresponding semi-circular distribution, particularly its 2kth moment which relates to non-crossing pair-partitions of the set {1, 2,... 2k}, has been extensively studied. Building upon existing knowledge, this paper contributes a broader extension that also reveals novel insights. Given an $n \times n$ symmetric matrix with independently distributed entries under certain assumptions, our study confirms that a limiting spectral distribution indeed exists with probability or certainty. However, this limit can be understood through more extensive partitions, giving rise to intriguing combinatorial problems. As a result, several existing spectral distribution theories, such as those concerning standard Wigner, Erdos-Renyi graph, heavy-tailed Wigner, and variance-profile Wigner matrices, can be derived or further refined.

Persuasive promotional videos are becoming increasingly influential in shaping consumer behavior and promoting social causes through various mediums such as e-commerce platforms and non-profit initiatives. Given the time-consuming and resource-intensive process of producing such high-quality videos by professional teams, the field of AI-powered video creation has gained momentum. This field is unique due to its interdisciplinary nature, which presents both opportunities and obstacles for AI models. A comprehensive survey of AI-powered video creation is presented here, which categorizes existing AI approaches into three main sections based on the scope of the video to be created, including single-image derivation, text-based sequencing, and mixed methods. Additionally, the challenges and future directions of AI-powered video creation are explored.

Recent studies have uncovered the prevalence of gradient masking in purportedly robust adversarial defenses. Consequently, defense strategies based on this concept are considered ineffective and can be readily bypassed. Notably, research into quantifying the occurrence and extent of gradient masking across different networks remains limited. This study addresses this gap by exploring the mensurability of gradient masking as a multi-dimensional rather than a binary phenomenon. In addition, we introduce novel metrics designed to evaluate the presence of gradient masking in diverse neural networks. These proposed metrics not only offer computational advantages but also facilitate comparative assessments between models without necessitating elaborate tailor-made attacks. Ultimately, our research demonstrates the efficacy of these metrics in gauging the prevalence of gradient masking across different network configurations.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation, notably in flat acoustic lenses and ultra-high frequency ultrasound imaging. This concept, however, has not yet been implemented at the MHz frequencies common in ultrasound imaging due to difficulties in fabricating complex microstructures. Advances in two-photon polymerization now enable precise manufacture of sub-wavelength structures in this range. However, shrinking structures in size introduces another challenge, where increased thermoviscous effects lead to considerable energy losses, which need to be factored into the design. This work introduces three novel microacoustic metagrating designs capable of refracting normally incident waves by approximately 35 degrees at 2 MHz, utilizing shape optimization techniques and the linearized Navier-Stokes equations. Using two-photon polymerization, we fabricated and experimentally validated microscopic acoustic metamaterials, successfully redirecting incident waves and verifying that a 0.2 wavelength thick microacoustic metagrating can efficiently control wave propagation in the mid-MHz frequency range.

Standard diffusion models can fail, particularly when influenced by correlations and variations, where mean squared displacements grow in a linear manner with time. We investigate the spread of a fractional Brownian population exhibiting time-dependent and diverse diffusion characteristics. Our primary objective is to establish the relationship between these individual characteristics and the population's spatial distribution as observed over time. We examine the applicability and limitations of this approach to a broad category of self-similar diffusion processes, utilizing a general framework that is subsequently applied to recognized processes such as Laplace diffusion, nonlinear diffusion, and their variants.

A fundamental theory is developed to describe both linear and Kerr nonlinear interactions between the modes of dielectric optical resonators, with the framework being applicable across various geometries and modes. The general approach allows for a wide range of phenomena resulting from linear interactions, scattering, and Kerr nonlinearity, such as mode coupling and phase modulation, to be analyzed. The developed theory is specifically applied to a waveguide with a microresonator in close proximity, enabling the computation of mode coupling and phase modulation terms. Furthermore, a dimensionless equation is derived to describe the dynamics of two identical counterpropagating modes in a loop resonator and, under the condition of mode identity, it is proven that cross-phase modulation is precisely twice as strong as self-phase modulation.

This paper builds upon established connections between global asymptotic controllability, stabilizability, and control Lyapunov functions in control systems that allow unbounded controls, encompassing polynomial control systems. Our analysis specifically addresses unbounded open-loop controls and discontinuous feedback stabilizers, which may lead to trajectories exhibiting chattering behavior near the target. A central aspect of our findings is the demonstration of the equivalence between global asymptotic controllability, stabilizability, and control Lyapunov functions in these control systems or their impulsive system extensions.

A recent study proposes a novel deep learning approach that utilizes generative adversarial networks to generate highly detailed turbulent velocity patterns from limited-resolution data across a range of Reynolds numbers. A specially designed multiscale model was utilized for high-fidelity velocity prediction and demonstrated significant speed improvements over traditional simulation methods. The research shows that this deep learning framework accurately replicates small-scale velocity details in turbulent flows at different Reynolds numbers, requiring a less extensive training dataset and delivering superior performance when compared to conventional interpolation methods. The model's efficiency was further highlighted by its ability to recreate complex turbulent velocity patterns in less than 10 milliseconds over an extended period.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently derives a non-radiative condition across inertial frames, consistent with the stability requirements of an atom, and establishes that this condition is analogous to certain relationships between charge, current, and the wave equations. The paper then demonstrates that these relationships lead to quantised electromagnetic field energy displaying the characteristics of the Balmer series.

The accuracy of machine learning models heavily relies on their confidence calibration. Deep neural network-based classifiers have a common issue of providing over-confident predictions, particularly when encountering unknown inputs. In order to account for this type of uncertainty, set-based classification methods, such as assigning probability distributions to multiple candidates, are typically employed. However, these approaches require the extraction of feature vectors for all potential targets, an unfeasible task in open-world scenarios. To tackle this limitation, we explore methods to shrink the decision region of well-classified samples within a single class energy-based model, thereby enhancing post-training confidence calibration. Our proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to baseline methods on several benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness without necessitating access to training data.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to support this research, new tools are being developed, including carefully crafted evaluation frameworks and benchmark environments. To address this need, we present Lifelong Learning Explorer (L2Explorer), a cutting-edge Unity-based environment that allows for continuous, flexible experimentation in a 3D, immersive exploration setting. L2Explorer is distinct from procedurally generated worlds, which often incorporate randomized components. Instead, we've developed a structured approach to lifelong learning through three key criteria: structured curricula, structured world complexity, and continuous transfer learning from one area of knowledge to another. We've assessed several continual learning methods using L2Explorer and found that as the complexity of the environments increases, the performance gains from transfer learning become more significant, and that models employing continual learning outperform those utilizing stochastic worlds in certain scenarios. Additionally, we've identified that open-ended data collection following new tasks can further boost generalization performance, and that data generated after encountering more challenging tasks is of higher quality, and can replace stochastic worlds in these specific cases.

Understanding business processes relies on process discovery methods, analyzing data trails to reveal underlying processes. As processes evolve over time, their corresponding models must adapt, otherwise they may inaccurately predict future behaviors. Our approach develops an algorithm to identify processes from event flows, represented as Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graphs, providing temporal process data and subsequently declarative process models. We validate this method through experiments and analyses, comparing it against changing real processes to ensure its effectiveness and accuracy. Our approach and associated test data are available online.

In one-dimensional quasiperiodic structures, certain types of wave propagation exhibit a sudden shift from localization to non-localization. Our theory and experimental results indicate that in one-dimensional photonic quasicrystals, light localization can transition back to non-localization at higher quasiperiodic modulation strengths for some states, representing an unusual phenomenon. Additionally, this occurrence can be understood through a mathematical model that represents dimerized interactions over extended distances.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, will be paired with the Keck All-sky Precision Adaptive-optics system to optimize performance. By covering the wavelength range from 0.81 micrometers to 2.45 micrometers, Liger combines multiple observing modes, offering various spatial scales and fields of view. However, Liger's data complexity necessitates a customized data processing system to refine its output in real-time, making it compatible with science-oriented data presentation tools. This processing system, called the Data Reduction System, will be responsible for delivering refined data to astronomers and uploading it to the Keck Observatory Archive. We have established a prototype of this data processing system and defined the communication interface with the relevant software systems at the observatory.

Optical systems that measure intensity in two-photon spatial modes are widely utilized in detecting defects in integrated circuits and semiconductor wafer inspection.
传统的缺陷检测系统无法识别微小缺陷, 需要放大被测物体, 这会带来视角放大, 焦点调整等额外挑战. 本研究揭示了一种新颖的应用方式, 可以将一维样本上的微小缺陷定位到超高分辨率的一维平面内, 从而在一维检测系统中实现无放大超分辨率效果. 我们通过实验验证了该方法可以将检测精度提升到波长量级.
This note provides an introduction to the interplay between Hodge-theoretic and geometric approaches to compactifying moduli spaces of algebraic varieties.

In the study of population dynamics, identifying early warning indicators for sudden population changes and the mechanisms that lead to regime shifts is highly beneficial. This paper focuses on a model consisting of a two-level ecosystem where two species of predators, competing for a common prey, engage in explicit interference. The model is reworked to display a singular perturbation with rapid prey movement and slower predator movement, allowing for a regime close to the singular Hopf bifurcation to be analyzed. Near this point, the model exhibits chaotic, mixed-mode oscillations, consisting of long-lasting, concatenated periods of small and large amplitude movements. These eventually transition into the model's steady-state equilibrium. To determine the initiating factors behind mixed-mode oscillations, the model is reduced to a model reentry locus, and the relationship between periods of MOs and oscillations of the fundamental branch of the nullcline is derived, ultimately linking the occurrence of MOs to the equilibrium stability.

Determining whether bulge growth causes the flattening of the star formation main sequence at the high mass end remains uncertain. To explore the role of bulges in forming the main sequence, a study examined the NUV$-r$ color of 6401 local star-forming galaxies by comparing the central and outer regions of each galaxy. Since NUV$-r$ color serves as a specific indicator of star formation rate, a distinction emerged when analyzing galaxies based on their stellar mass. At stellar masses less than $10^{10.3}M_{\sun}$, there is only a small color difference between the central and outer NUV$-r$. Above this threshold, however, a more significant difference in color becomes apparent, indicating the central bulge in these massive galaxies is on average more mature. Observing the behavior of galaxies based on their S\'ersic index $n$ further revealed that the role of bulges in creating the flattening of the star formation main sequence at the high mass end remains unclear. When considering galaxies with an S\'ersic index greater than 2.5, the external NUV$-r$ relation starts to flatten at a stellar mass of $10^{10.3}M_{\sun}$, which contradicts the expectation that star formation suppression within bulges is responsible for this flattening.

This paper conducts a sentiment analysis across languages, examining the
emotional content of news articles using both few-shot and zero-shot learning
techniques. The primary objective is to categorize Croatian news articles as
expressing positive, negative, or neutral sentiment, employing a dataset from
Slovene. The underlying model is a multilingual BERT-based system, pre-trained
on three languages: English, Slovene, and Croatian. The paper investigates
various setups utilizing datasets from two languages and presents a straightforward
multi-task model to accomplish sentiment classification. The assessment involves
zero-shot and few-shot learning approaches within single-task and multi-task
experiments for both Slovene and Croatian.

Recently, cache coherence protocols based on self-invalidation and self-downgrade have gained more recognition due to their minimalistic design, potential for increased performance efficiency, and reduced energy consumption. However, these protocols introduce memory instruction reordering, leading to additional, unforeseen program behaviors. This study explores the impact of such unexpected behaviors on data flow information in C and C++ through a comprehensive analysis utilizing the Memory Model Checker (MMC) and a large custom dataset. Our examination reveals substantial security implications arising from speculation-based leaks, which can be mitigated with suitable mitigations, yet overlooks traditional information flow control guarantees, especially those provided by labels and flags. Our investigation demonstrates that unannotated programs are particularly vulnerable to massive speculation-based leaks, while low-speculation hardware can still prevent labeled programs from experiencing information flow control violations. Moreover, program downgrading can help restore protected flags and prevent data label downgrades, while also mitigating the introduction of unexpected label downgrades. Overall, our research indicates that the combination of self-invalidating, self-downgrading memory operations, and explicit annotation of memory instructions can effectively manage data and label information flows, especially in conjunction with hardware supporting low-speculation behavior.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset with a size near 2k, then A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we aim to enhance this by limiting the number of possible summands available from subset B. It's shown that if subsets A and B, of size k, meet the criterion that for every four-element subset of B, the sumset A plus that subset doesn't exceed 2k, it follows that A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions.

Consider a fractional Brownian motion $B^{H}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with Hurst index $H$ in the interval $(0,1)$. Let $f$ be a Borel function from $[0,1]$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, and $A$ a Borel subset of $[0,1]$. Conditions will be established under which the image $(B^{H}+f)(A)$ has a positive Lebesgue measure or a non-empty interior. This is achieved through investigating properties of the occupation measure's density for $(B^{H}+f)$, particularly proving that if the parabolic Hausdorff dimension of $f$ exceeds $Hd$, then its density function is square-integrable, or if $A$'s Hausdorff dimension surpasses $Hd$, then its density function admits a continuous version, thus providing a result already mentioned.

Using Dirac's time-dependent variational principle, we establish a simple H\'enon-Heiles model based on semiclassical mechanics. A two-body trial wavefunction in the form of Hatree-type is applied, leading to the derivation of an effective Hamiltonian in the context of Jackiw-Kerman theory. The calculations yield results indicating that quantum fluctuations can provoke chaotic behavior in regions of the H\'enon-Heiles system that classically remain stable.

X-ray images contain subtle cues that indicate signs of ICU admission, improving
prediction models can facilitate personalized healthcare plans, reducing unnecessary ICU
utilization, in this research we explore features hidden within X-ray images related to
ICU admission, initially, we investigate whether employing a high-capacity model is
essential to extract these features; a surprising finding revealed that medium and low
capacity models perform nearly as well as high capacity models. Secondly, we investigate
how to effectively utilize ICU-related features from X-rays for enhancement of feature
fusion models. Our research shows that combining a deep learning model with manual
features can lead to more accurate ICU admission predictions. Furthermore, we
introduce a novel, simple method to enhance feature fusion using both multi-modal and
mono-modal models, in this context KENN is found more effective than other hand-crafted
features. We open-source our code for feature extraction and preparation at this link:
https://github.com/cjy1991/ICU-admission-features-from-Chest-X-ray,  for your
reference, we evaluate several prediction models through four independent tests with a
variety of datasets, our results indicate that GCNet outperforms other models in AUC
metrics both in our test A with 0.8334 and in the publicly available test sets B with 0.7411,
C, and D with 0.8419,

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals struggle to contribute effectively. Our proposed framework, Spatially-Aware Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (SABRA), mitigates the impact of false positives in VRD tasks. To counter the imbalance, SABRA incorporates Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), which divides proposals into distinct sub-classes based on difficulty and samples a balanced distribution accordingly. By employing this strategy, BNPS yields an optimized model performance and a notable decrease in false positives. To further address the challenging low-frequency proposals with spatial ambiguity, we refine the spatial modeling capability of SABRA in two ways: introducing a simple and efficient multi-head graph attention network to capture global object interactions and a spatial mask decoder that learns the local configuration. Our approach demonstrates superior performance compared to the current state-of-the-art methods across three datasets for human-object interaction and visual relationship detection.

This study offers a supervised action recognition solution that's effective even in the absence of light. We've obtained promising results by testing our approach on the ARID dataset, a significantly smaller and darker collection of video data. Notably, previous action recognition methods typically relied on well-lit datasets such as Kinetics and HMDB51. Our results indicate that our technique achieves remarkable accuracy despite being trained on a much reduced and poorly lit dataset of video sequences. We've experimented with multiple training and prediction methods including cross-domain techniques, as well as introducing an efficient yet straightforward approach for frame selection. Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed method surpasses existing benchmark models with a significant margin of 11% improvement.

This report outlines the development of a novel Content Addressable Parallel Processor, built with a Field Programmable Gate Array. Although content-addressable memories have been successfully implemented on FPGAs, our design uniquely captures Caxton C. Foster's pioneering ideas on parallel processing, incorporating the concepts of simultaneous parallel writes and the merging of output values – features commonly omitted in typical CAM applications like network routing. The resulting system allows a host computer to interface with the CAPP over USB/UART using a simple serial communication protocol, which has been effectively demonstrated with a Python-based driver.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of three galaxy cores at $\rm z=2.91$ within a massive galaxy group, yielding high-resolution infrared and submillimeter data. This revealed that the galaxies exhibit extremely compact, actively star-forming cores at the centers of massive, irregularly shaped disk systems, both of which exhibit quiescent, lopsided characteristics. Consequently, these cores appear to be in the process of transitioning from disk-like galaxies to bulge-dominated systems. Furthermore, we speculate that one of these systems is experiencing ongoing accretion, as indicated by an external infrared jet. Furthermore, we observe that these systems commonly occur within massive galaxy group environments, often residing in the outer regions and associations of these groups, and within nearly merger-stable environments, far from major collision courses. This implies that tidal forces and tidal dissipation may fuel starbursts, and that these mechanisms, in tandem with gas funneling via vertical bar dynamics, contribute to the creation of bulges within these galaxies.

We re-examine and revise the predictions of the Universal Texture Zero (UTZ) flavour model as initially presented in the study arXiv:1710.01741. The revision is made with reference to more accurate experimental restrictions and refined numerical analysis methods. Specifically, our team developed an in-house Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to extensively evaluate the viable parameter range of the UTZ model, encompassing primary and secondary contributions in its effective operator expansion. Furthermore, we obtained for the first time precise UTZ predictions for previously underdetermined CP-violating phases of lepton interactions, and related neutrino mass characterizing ratio observables, that could be probed via oscillations, beta decay, and cosmological processes. Consequently, our revised analysis significantly surpasses the initial analysis and confirms that the UTZ theory remains a coherent and compelling flavour theory. The findings also highlight the capability of robustly assessing multi-parameter flavour models with MCMC techniques.

We examine a specific nonlinear elliptic equation in R^N, where N is 5 or greater. No studies on the periodicity of its solutions have been done previously, so we explore related issues by making some key assumptions about a given function, Q(y), which is periodic and has a minimum value at zero. We demonstrate the existence of a sequence of bubbling solutions that mimic the standard solution for a related equation, as well as the absence of solutions for certain bounded domains, for sufficiently large dilation parameters, where the domain does not support standard solutions for the associated equation.

Current cutting-edge neural code models excel at generating individual code segments but often struggle with complex tasks, like entire function creation. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that leverages static code analysis for feedback. Our framework for neural code generation uses data-flow analysis to validate partial codes and feeds back the results to the underlying decoder. We specifically applied this approach to the task of producing Python functions from descriptive texts, and found substantial improvements in the quality of code produced by our system compared to the baseline system without static feedback. We observed that our method also yields better performance on more challenging test cases. We further enhanced our model by replacing basic data-flow analysis with a more competent programmer simulation, and found even more significant results.

Recently discovered sensitive detectors of plastic scintillators have enable exploration of solar neutron beta decay as a source of plasma pollution. Analysis of data from the SOHO and STEREO spacecraft revealed significant reductions in solar neutron decay protons on October 30 - November 4, 2004. This period followed an event on November 1, 2004 when a high energy solar burst resulted in the detection of a single particle at both spacecraft. The probability of this occurrence happening by chance is extremely low, at less than one percent. The findings suggest that solar plasma pollution can be significantly reduced with high energy solar bursts containing protons, neutrons and electrons.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows that, in the tensor mode, the divergence-based model aligns with the quasi-hydrodynamic quasi-local energy model when considering gauge invariant quantities. Furthermore, we've discussed the implications of our results for numerical hydrodynamic simulations.

Real-time anomaly detection in continuous data streams presents difficulties for conventional and advanced methods due to shifting concepts and ongoing learning requirements. Existing approaches, such as using hash functions or nearest neighbors with fixed memory, can struggle to accommodate frequent fluctuations, remove smooth outliers, and adapt to deep neural network architectures. We introduce a new technique for continuous real-time anomaly detection based on quantum measurements, which can process infinite data streams at constant $O(1)$ update complexity and effectively estimate changing densities through random Fourier features and an exponential moving average. This approach was thoroughly evaluated by comparing it to 12 prominent algorithms for real-time anomaly detection on 12 diverse data streams.

A pivotal question arises when a court possesses information that an individual knows the passcode to a device, prompting the court to compel the person to provide access. Notable figures, including Elon Musk, have publicly stanced that forcing someone to reveal their passcode constitutes an infringement on their Fifth Amendment rights, as it would set a concerning precedent. Conversely, some legal experts argue that passcodes, unlike private messages, aren't inherently confidential and thus don't warrant such protection. We put this to the test by conducting three experiments involving more than 1,000 university students, assessing their perceptions of a court's legitimacy, security, and the ethical implications of such actions. Our findings suggest that individuals view passcodes as inherently confidential, and attempting to bypass them forces, rather than facilitating, compliance. Additionally, we observe that the age of participants affects these outcomes, offering valuable insights that could inform future legal decisions.

We have developed a comprehensive model that enables simulation of the measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) process. It can predict real-world observations and outcomes in scenarios involving linear channel loss, including the associated gain levels, error rates in different measurement bases, and final key rates. Our model is versatile and can be applied to various MDI-QKD implementations that employ convex source states or diverse coding techniques. As such, it is an invaluable resource for analyzing and evaluating the performance of different MDI-QKD protocols.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes that have limited connectivity.

A previously developed method by Baker achieved PTAS on various graph classes including planar graphs. Further, Romero, Wrochna, and Zivny developed a parameterized PTAS for some graph classes that have higher levels of connectivity. Their approach was limited to levels less than $\log n$.

In this research, we achieve a PTAS for solving certain general-valued CSPs that have high connectivity. We do this by creating an approximate polynomial tree-decomposition of inputs that maintains representation of at least some pairwise constraints. This technique builds upon Baker's polynomial tree-depth approach and yields a PTAS for CSPs on graph classes with connectivity levels that grow at a rate similar to $\log n$. We refine this rate to at least $O(\sqrt{\log \log n})$ for specific CSP instances.

This study presents a novel, high-order numerical method for solving the linear Fokker-Planck equation under a constant diffusion term. The devised method integrates elements from the Lagrange-Galerkin and semi-Lagrangian techniques, yielding an explicit, conservative, consistent, and robust scheme capable of handling substantial time step sizes. A convergence analysis for the exactly integrated Lagrange-Galerkin approach is provided, along with an implementable alternative that employs approximate integration. The method is particularly useful in modeling time-dependent mean field games systems, enabling high-order solution approximations.

Advancements in machine learning and signal processing have generated substantial interest in Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), which excel at solving complex, engineering-driven problems. Despite their success, a key challenge remains in understanding how DNNs reach their solutions. This particular survey focuses on the explanation, interpretation, and visualization of DNN decisions and internal workings. By examining multiple explanation strategies from diverse perspectives, this survey aims to deepen the insight into the explanation and visualization of DNNs solutions and functioning.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to angular momentum conservation principles. To validate our findings, we updated the constraints based on spectroscopic surface measurements, verified that the detected oscillation patterns align with the star's chemical composition, and confirmed that the star is not being spun up by a rapidly rotating companion through modeling. Additionally, we explored whether a past interaction with a giant planet in its system might have accounted for the unusual surface rotation profile detected in this star.

Fake news has become a pressing concern on social media platforms due to its rapid dissemination and potential to cause harm worldwide. Although machine learning models have been successful in detecting false information, especially when large amounts of labeled data are available, their effectiveness significantly declines when they are applied to emerging events. This limitation is attributed to the scarcity of labeled samples for new events. In response, we introduce a meta-learning approach that automatically learns low-dimensional embeddings from label-free captioned images, accurately identifying false news in both known and emerging events without requiring any label information. By incorporating a meta neural process module, our framework efficiently handles the uncertainty associated with unknown events, allowing it to detect false news with high accuracy. Our experiments on two diverse datasets showcase significant improvements, including notable enhancements on the Google Images and Flickr datasets when they are used to represent unknown events.

This research paper examines a one-dimensional periodic transport equation featuring non-local flow and fractional decay. The equation in question is given by $$
u_{t}-(Hu)_{x}u_{x}+\kappa\Lambda^{\alpha}u=0,\quad (t,x)\in R^{+}\times S.
$$
Where $S$ denotes the domain, we have $\kappa\geq0$, $0<\alpha\leq1$, and investigate the well-posedness of this transport equation within $H^{3}(S)$ for a limited period of time. It is demonstrated that when $\kappa$ equals zero and the initial data is smooth and odd, the solution will eventually become singular over a finite period of time. Additionally, we find that introducing a weak dissipation term $\kappa\Lambda^{\alpha}u$ also leads to the formation of singularity in a finite amount of time.

This paper investigates the age of information (AoI) in a discrete-time status updating system that employs the Ber/G/1/1 queue. We demonstrate that utilizing a two-dimensional state vector which simultaneously monitors AoI and packet age enables derivation of the stationary AoI distribution via analysis of a constituted stochastic process. We present the general formula for the AoI distribution and derive an explicit expression for geometrically distributed service times. A comparison between discrete and continuous-time systems reveals the impact of AoI on system performance under various conditions. We also explore the relationship between discrete and continuous-time systems by establishing the approximate formula for continuous-time AoI distribution.

This work delves into various quantum algebras that arise from a special type of set-theoretic solution to the Yang-Baxter equation and their 'q-analogue' counterparts, also providing common characteristics that these algebras share in terms of quasi-bialgebras and twists. By establishing that set-theoretic and q-analogue solutions produce the same specific types of algebras and by identifying additional constraints for their 'q-deformed' counterparts, this research greatly expands our current understanding of set-theoretic solutions and their quantum equivalents, revealing new general patterns in the field.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible in four-dimensional space if certain conditions are met concerning the sizes and their factorization. Additionally, in binary GCM quadruples, possible sizes are postulated as unlimited, which is confirmed for sizes 78x78 and a few scattered instances, whereas all positive integers below 1000 can be covered in a one-dimensional space of a quaternary GCM quad.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics, and it can rival Coulomb interactions to give rise to intricate phenomena.
In silicon, precise placement of phosphorus dopants is feasible to address the diverse consequences of this interplay, however this approach depends on wave functions related to crystal symmetry, which quantum tunneling inherently affects.
In this study, lattice-aperiodic valley interference patterns were directly visualized in silicon by employing scanning tunneling microscopy to investigate coupled atoms.
The examination reveals the significance of valley exchange narrowing the energy spectrum for certain configurations, a phenomenon without counterpart in spin exchange narrowing that is vital for quantum sensing and computation.
The findings demonstrate that understanding tunneling is crucial when designing devices based on silicon quantum bits and hindered quantum computations due to coupling-dependent coupling.
The investigation reveals the characteristics of wave function engineering in silicon, a crucial aspect for advancing this field.

Complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components typically adhere to straightforward and universal principles, which underpin their intricate behavior. Despite graph neural networks offering valuable insights for studying such systems, there's still much we don't understand about them when they operate within high-dimensional phases spaces. This paper presents a novel graph neural network architecture tailored for dynamical systems, which effectively integrates time-series data with pairwise interactions between components. Our approach, called Dynamic Edge-Attention GNN, outperforms existing methods in forecasting system behavior, accurately reconstructing their underlying structure, and robustly handles systems with varying components. These results highlight the potential of machine learning techniques to generate definitive, interpretable models of complex dynamical systems.

We introduce an infinite family of recursive formulas for calculating the counts of binary integer partitions that fulfill specific divisibility criteria, establishing relationships among these counts via cumulative sums. These formulas have a meaningful interpretation within the framework of graded polynomial rings and enable us to derive computations related to homology modules in the context of stable homotopy theory, utilizing the properties of the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra.

A cutting-edge, minimally invasive therapy called Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) treats seizures caused by epilepsy in a specific brain area, the mesial temporal lobe. Evaluating the effectiveness of this treatment requires analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT, which can be achieved by accurately defining the treated region through image processing. Although deep learning techniques offer high precision in defining this region, training them requires a large amount of data which can be hard to obtain for a new and emerging treatment such as LITT. In response, this paper proposes an innovative framework called Progressive Brain Lesion Synthesis, consisting of multiple stages to artificially create more training data with various characteristics, thereby enhancing the precision of the therapy evaluation. Furthermore, the paper includes a design for encoding external information that can aid in training and improving segmentation results by integrating a condition and mask embedding block, resulting in better outcomes when compared to common image processing methods, according to experimental data.

Strong nonlocality, a phenomenon where systems demonstrate nonlocality without entanglement, can be seen in multipartite states with certain properties. Unextendible product bases (UPBs) have shown nonlocality without entanglement in previous research, and their strong quantum nonlocality is therefore a topic of interest. However, many UPBs of minimal size cannot demonstrate this strong quantum nonlocality. In this research, a series of UPBs of various larger sizes for systems of three and four parties were constructed in dimensions of $d_A, d_B, d_C, d_D \geq 3$. It was also shown that these UPBs have strong quantum nonlocality, answering open questions from Halder and others, and providing a connection between this phenomenon and UPBs. To locally distinguish one such UPB in $3 \otimes 3 \otimes 4$, an entanglement-assisted protocol was proposed, using less entanglement than previously known protocols.

The speed at which massive spectroscopic surveys collect data directly corresponds to the number of optical fibers used in each observation. This paper assesses complete coordination methods for astrophotographers by using a real-world example from the Fifth Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We conducted our tests using ASTROLAB, a customized telescope developed at the University of Valencia. By comparing different safe-coordination algorithms on the telescope, we found that our newly proposed method, CASP, performs as well as or better than existing algorithms across various types of astronomical targets. CASP's improved performance will enable forastero-like telescopes to collect a larger number of observations per run, resulting in more efficient and cost-effective data collection.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for efficient program analysis and verification, leveraging graph transformation rules to ease these tasks. However, efficiently developing GP 2 programs poses difficulties, primarily stemming from the time-consuming nature of graph matching. To overcome this limitation, the GP 2 framework incorporates a type of rule that guarantees a time complexity of O(n), along with an associated technique to convert ordinary graph-based rules into these specialized rules. Despite O(n) complexity being common in programming, it is not inherently suitable for graph-based methods. To address this disparity, the GP 2 compiler integrates elements from both traditional and graph-based compilation processes, resulting in the creation of the Improved GP 2 Compiler, which can successfully compile both graph-based and specialized rules.

Dimensionality reduction in high-dimensional data is effectively managed by a technique called feature extraction. Self-supervised learning's prominent method, contrastive learning, has gained considerable interest recently. Our research introduces a novel, all-encompassing framework that integrates contrastive learning for both unsupervised and supervised feature extraction tasks. The framework's initial step constructs unique contrastive learning graphs to differentiate between similar and dissimilar data points, with a focus on optimizing a contrastive loss function to obtain the projection matrix. The framework's capability to handle similar and dissimilar data enables the integration of unsupervised and supervised feature extraction techniques. We further developed three specific methods: an unsupervised contrastive learning technique and two supervised contrastive learning approaches. Our framework's superiority is demonstrated through comprehensive numerical experiments conducted on five real-world datasets, resulting in performance improvements over existing methods.

We establish an infinite sequence of locally arc-transitive graphs characterized by a unique property: their automorphism groups partition vertices into two distinct orbits while exhibiting quasiprimativity on just one orbit, specifically within a class of twisted wreath structures. Our findings expand upon a framework initially proposed by Giudici, Li, and Praeger by providing an infinite number of examples classified under the star normal quotient twisted wreath category for locally arc-transitive graphs.

Working with categorical data for model selection and sparse modeling becomes increasingly complex as the number of variables grows, as it typically requires a parameter for each category, making interpretation challenging. Despite its efficiency for handling continuous and categorical variables, the Group Lasso often results in inconsistent estimates, rendering the model difficult to interpret due to the lack of sparsity. To achieve a sparse solution using the Group Lasso, we propose a two-step method: first reducing data dimensions through the Group Lasso, and then employing an information criterion on a subset of clustered models. This algorithm's performance is evaluated under high-dimensional conditions and compared with state-of-the-art methods using synthetic and real-world datasets, showing its superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy and model size.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. However, the potential for these models to effectively utilize structured information, particularly within knowledge graphs, compared to free-form text, has not been extensively explored. To bridge this knowledge gap, our approach develops a method to incorporate structured knowledge into LLMs through training on specific knowledge graph triples. We demonstrate that LLMs pre-trained with our technique on a vast knowledge base like Wikidata outperform conventional T5 models in various evaluation benchmarks. Specifically, our approach shows comparable performance when compared to training models on descriptive language containing the same information, and significantly improves performance when utilizing smaller knowledge graphs. One key advantage of this method is the absence of a requirement to synchronize knowledge graphs with text data, making it highly suitable for large-scale knowledge graphs.

This article examines spatially nonlocal diffusion models, where interactions are limited to a finite distance $\delta$ and investigates how they are defined in a bounded area with various boundary conditions representing inhomogeneous data. The article compares their solutions with classical PDE models under specific localization limits, as well as how rescaled fractional kernels relate to inhomogeneous fractional boundary value problems. These discussions shed light on the challenges and issues that arise in nonlocal problems with inhomogeneous data within bounded domains.

When capturing panoramic scenes, individuals usually align their cameras parallel to the direction of gravity. Many portable devices, including smartphones and tablets, are fitted with sensors that can accurately track the direction of gravity. Based on this assumption, the axis of cameras in such configurations can be assumed to be aligned or adjusted accordingly, thus reducing the necessary alignment parameters to one dimension. Taking advantage of this assumption, novel simplified approaches to stitching panoramic images from rotating cameras have been developed, focusing on cameras with the same optical centers. Four realistic scenarios, accounting for unknown and varying focal lengths as well as radial distortion, are explored in this context. Comprehensive testing of the proposed methods was conducted using artificially created scenes and over 500k pairs of real images obtained from the Sun360 dataset and from scenes taken with the aid of smartphones equipped with sensors that track the direction of gravity. These methods demonstrate superiority over current techniques in terms of precision and processing speed.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

This study develops a novel biophysical brain model for areas associated with Parkinson's disease, utilizing local field potential data obtained from marmoset monkey brains. Parkinson's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, disrupts normal basal ganglia-thalamus-cortex function. Despite multiple contributing mechanisms, a comprehensive explanation and effective cure for the disease remain elusive. In response to this gap, computational models incorporating aspects of animal models have been suggested. Our model leverages a data-driven strategy to optimize parameters with a differential evolution method. Successful outcomes from the evolved models closely matched observed firing rates and spectral characteristics of local field potentials from healthy and diseased marmoset brain data. Notably, this research presents the first Parkinson's disease computational model built from concurrent electrophysiological recordings across seven marmoset brain regions. The findings suggest our proposed model can facilitate the exploration of disease mechanisms and contribute to the development of novel therapeutic approaches. Additionally, it may be applied to various computational neuroscience challenges where biological data can inform multi-scale brain circuit models.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via anti-aliasing. The proposed method effectively approximates the anti-aliased appearance of line joins while reducing draw calls to one triangle per join, thus optimizing rendering. The novel solution is implemented and validated against an industry standard map application, demonstrating its viability when integrated into real-world mapping scenarios. The source code for this technique has been made publicly available for examination.

Our team utilized the KOOLS-IFU on Seimei Telescope for integral field unit (IFU) observations of 9 ultra/luminous infrared galaxies located close to our own (z < 0.04) and participating in the GOALS survey. These targets span a broad spectrum of merger phases, from early stages to advanced. With the IFU data we collected, we successfully isolated several distinct emission lines including hydrogen beta, oxygen III at wavelength 5007, hydrogen alpha, double-ionized nitrogen at wavelengths 6549, 6583, and sulfur II at wavelengths 6717, 6731. Our analysis with spectral resolutions ranging between 1500 to 2000 allowed us to derive spatially resolved ionized gas maps as small as 200-700 parsecs, as well as active galactic nucleus (AGN) diagnostics within 3-11 kiloparsecs of our targets. Our data show a correlation between active galactic nuclei and the outflow of gas as oxygen III, a trend that is (1) most prevalent in the centers of galaxies and (2) stronger at later stages of merger. For example, during late stages of merger we measured an outflow 1.5 times as powerful as during early stages of merger. These observations imply a relationship between the interaction of galaxy mergers and the outflow of gas that may influence the formation

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), enabling smoother interpolation results. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the method's efficiency and accuracy.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct characteristics that distinguish different weather conditions.
Existing approaches to this problem are largely confined to specific environments and only tackle the classification of bad weather conditions.
We address these limitations by introducing the WEDA dataset, presenting a novel framework for extracting multi-scale features through the Unsupervised Weather Detection Architecture (WEDA), and demonstrating that our method outperforms state-of-the-art strategies across the entire spectrum of weather conditions.

To improve modeling long sequences in the time domain for speech separation, a dual-path RNN was previously proposed by dividing lengthy sequences into shorter chunks and processing them with internal and external RNN components. Building upon this work, a Dual-Path Convolution Recurrent Network (DPCRN) model is presented here by integrating the dual-path RNN with Convolution Recurrent Networks. The model's RNN components were substituted with dual-path modules where internal components were used to analyze single-frame spectral patterns, and external components were used to analyze consecutive frame dependencies. Notably, with only 0.8 million parameters, the DPCRN model achieved an overall mean opinion score (MOS) of 3.57 in the wideband scenario of the Interspeech 2021 DNS challenge. Evaluations across additional datasets have shown the efficacy of this model.

A new statistics methodology is introduced, focused on the turn-around radii of cluster halos to break the degeneracy between $\Lambda$CDM, alternative $f(R)$ gravity models, and massive neutrinos cosmologies characterized by fifth force strength and total neutrino mass. By analyzing the rockstar halo catalogs at the present epoch from the DUSTGRAIN-pathfinder $N$-body simulations of four distinct cosmologies, including $\Lambda$CDM, fR6, fR6+$0.06$eV, and fR5+$0.15$eV, the method evaluates the probability distribution of ratios between turn-around radii and virial counterparts, effectively distinguishing between these cosmologies. It is found that fR6 and fR5+$0.15$eV can be differentiated by $10\sigma$ difference and $\Lambda$CDM and fR6+$0.06$eV can be differentiated by $3.2\sigma$ difference. Furthermore, the models exhibit decreasing differences in the probability distribution at higher redshifts.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models hold promise in refining the simulation of atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations. A dynamic framework by nature, this method eliminates several of the parameterizations typically used to model convection, yet implementing this approach demands resolving multiple length and time scales across the different fluid components. Before embarking on such a venture, single-column models incorporating two-fluid frameworks must first be developed. This study employs horizontal multi-fluid models consisting of two interacting fluid components within the Rayleigh-Benard convection setting as an idealized test case for atmospheric convection. We explore the application of these models by comparing their results to those from single-fluid models, paying particular attention to characteristics such as total convection speed, individual fluid velocities, temperature fluctuations, and the distribution of kinetic energy. Findings indicate that, under specific conditions, multi-fluid models exhibit more realistic convection patterns, closely resembling observed convection in laboratory settings.

We investigate three separate Jaynes-Cummings systems, with two of the systems having correlated atoms, but the third system is unconnected. Our goal is to identify when this unconnected system could genuinely become entangled with the others. Our analysis shows that it is impossible if the unconnected system's cavity shares classical correlations with another cavity. Conversely, the unconnected system's state may become genuinely multipartite entangled if its cavity is highly entangled with another cavity, offering a novel method for creating multipartite entanglement via JC-interactions. Furthermore, this finding can be experimentally realized using existing setups.

The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) is one of the primary detectors in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, tracking particle interactions resulting from high-energy collisions. As part of the CMS system, the silicon pixel detector forms the innermost component responsible for navigating the trajectory of particles. Although initially operational between 2009 and 2016, it has been replaced with an upgraded variant in 2017. During a preceding period of shutdown for the LHC, an upgraded forward pixel detector prototype featuring a novel readout system and third disk was introduced, integrating eight pilot blades built using advanced digital readout chips. Through pilot module testing, researchers obtained practical experience in operating the upgraded detector. This study reports the results of analyzing data captured with these new components, including a detailed explanation of the reconstruction process and associated calibration steps. Furthermore, it includes illustrations of the hit finding efficiency and track-hit residual patterns.

A method is presented for computing the Kall\'en-Lehmann spectral density from lattice QCD data, which remains gauge invariant. The proposed method is tested on the SU(2) glueball spectrum for specific quantum numbers and at varying lattice spacings. The study employs published data to determine the spectral density and the glueball spectrum. The results for the ground state mass are consistent with the conventional approach using exponential correlations. Additionally, preliminary indications of excited states within the spectrum can be derived from the spectral density.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled a new set of training and testing data from these sources. An
LSTM-based classification model was developed to determine the sentiment expressed in
individual tweets. The model's performance was assessed using the newly created dataset.

A nonlinear interaction occurs between electromagnetic fields in quantum electrodynamics, resulting in vacuum polarization. This interaction can lead to a new field of non-linear electrodynamics, where fundamental photons can interact with one another. By applying nonlinear self-interaction concepts to charged black holes in anti-de Sitter space, we examine how photon interaction influences black hole physics. Utilizing the non-linear Born-Infon action, we derive an equation describing the relationship between the electric charge and the photon interaction, thus, we explore how this influence impacts black hole metrics. In our analysis, we maintain mass, temperature, and horizon radius constant to identify an optimal photon interaction strength that maximizes charge. Maintaining temperature and photon interaction constant, we reveal that the relationship between mass and charge exhibits a minimum mass threshold dependent on horizon radius. Furthermore, we maintain mass and photon interaction constant to investigate how the temperature varies as a function of horizon radius, ultimately determining the stability of the black hole. Notably, we observe that an increase in optimal photon interaction leads to a reduction in the ratio of heat capacity to mass, ultimately stabilizing the black hole. Surprisingly, we maintain that shadow geometry exhibits minimal sensitivity to photon interaction, with only a 0.5 percent variation observed.

Reconstructing a quantum state of continuous-variable systems like the radiation field is complicated, mainly due to the high dimensionality of its Hilbert space. Multiple approaches have been proposed for state reconstruction, including conventional methods and machine learning applications, yet there's no universally effective protocol for deriving the Wigner function from an optical tomogram of an arbitrary light state. We demonstrate that specific non-classical effects such as the generation of entanglement and onset of quantum synchronization are directly reflected in distinct patterns of optical tomograms, eliminating the need for full state reconstruction in these instances.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue models have achieved significant breakthroughs.
Despite this, developing a scalable chat system poses a major challenge due to
the requirement for substantial human-human dialogue data to support features
like persona, style, or safety. To tackle this issue, our work aims to introduce
role constraints to open-domain dialogue systems, enabling them to consistently
demonstrate specified characteristics in human conversations. Achieving this involves
two key steps: first, a novel data filtering approach is proposed to derive closed
scopes from large-scale open-domain dialogue datasets; followed by our development
of a role-conditioned open-domain dialogue system in response to user queries,
utilizing sampled sub-datasets and auxiliary role specified conditions. Our experiments
conducted on two large-scale dialogue datasets, WeChat 2.0 and OpenSubtitles, demonstrate
that our proposed method effectively builds effective open-domain dialogue systems.

Farmers utilize pesticides to minimize crop losses, but their effectiveness often depends on analyzing average treatment outcomes, which may not accurately reflect the best approach given the variability seen in production markets. To accurately compare pesticide treatments, we developed a statistical method that accounts for data variability and evaluates the probability of achieving a satisfactory outcome. Using strawberry disease management as a case study, we applied this method to evaluate the benefits of more intensive treatment practices. Our analysis revealed that the additional cost of these practices could be justified, with a 95% likelihood of obtaining excellent results, exceeding the initial cost investment. Furthermore, this approach allows for an equitable comparison between more intensive pesticide practices and reduced alternatives using integrated pest management techniques.

360-degree streaming videos offer engaging and immersive experiences but
require significant bandwidth. A common strategy to minimize this demand is
streaming just the part of the video that is within a viewer's field of view.
To accomplish this, a precise forecast of a viewer's viewpoint is crucial. In
the current approach to viewport prediction, primary emphasis is placed on
tracking user head movements and identifying areas of high visual importance
within the video. Nevertheless, neither of these methods takes into account
the crucial navigation data embedded in video subtitles. Such data, particularly
found in 360-degree virtual tourism videos, can significantly steer user
attention toward certain parts of the video. Consequently, it indicates that
video subtitles have substantial value in enhancing viewport prediction. To
incorporate this aspect, a new subtitle-driven prediction model, known as SPAP-VR,
has been devised. This model integrates navigation data from subtitles with
head movement information and visual importance within video frames to precisely
predict user viewports. Numerous externally sourced tests demonstrate the
effectiveness of SPAP-VR in predicting viewports. Additionally, the impact of
subtitle navigation data on model performance has been thoroughly examined in
these tests.

Tensor network methods have commonly been utilized in modeling different types of equilibrium and non-equilibrium situations. However, these techniques faced a critical challenge as their algorithms generally necessitated a small bond dimension at sufficiently low temperatures or time points, despite a fundamental requirement for approximating thermal states and time-evolved systems where the bond dimension is directly related to system size. This issue was tackled by constructing a specific class of objects that are able to accurately represent the thermal expectation values and time-evolved behavior for local observables in any scenario, where the bond dimension is completely independent of the system's size and is only determined by the temperature or elapsed time. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of these constructed objects in approximating thermal correlations and expectation values following a quantum quench event.

We develop a decoupling theory for a diverse range of polynomial equations and surface types, including spheres, hyperboloids, ellipsoids, and even complex hypersurfaces defined by $x^3+y^3+z^3+w^3=0$. Our approach centers on creating simpler, comparable geometric structures broken down by size, with key properties of curvature and flatness for each segment. This allows us to derive similar approximation schemes for both quadratic and non-quadratic surfaces, resulting in comprehensive 'decoupling inequalities' for a broad class of hypersurfaces.

In this research, we establish a precise inequality relating anisotropic mean curvature and capacity in the L^p norm, applicable to any bounded area in R^n with smooth borders.
As a result, we derive inequalities including an anisotropic Willmore inequality, a sharp anisotropic Minkowski inequality, and a sharp volumetric anisotropic Minkowski inequality. Our proof involves a novel approach in nonlinear potential theory recently described in the reference provided.

The Microscope space test for the weak equivalence principle involves measuring tiny differences in the acceleration of two test masses as they orbit the Earth. Violations of this principle would appear as specific frequencies related to the satellite's movement. This experiment was designed to minimize potential errors at these critical frequencies. Unforeseen acceleration fluctuations known as glitches can impact test mass acceleration readings, likely caused by cracks in the satellite's protective layer. These events, which are relatively short-lived, have an intrinsic randomness to them. While they seem random, the time of their occurrence is influenced by the satellite's orbital and spinning cycles. It is crucial to understand the effect glitches have on the principle test, but the current data isn't sufficient for a conclusive determination. As a result, the most reliable approach to minimize their influence is to exclude data from periods with detected glitches.

We examine a rigid structure composed of two active Brownian particles that interact in an activity gradient. We demonstrate analytically that the position of the dimer varies based on the angle between the particles and accumulates either at areas with high activity levels or low activity levels. This corresponds to chemotaxis and antichemotaxis respectively. Some dimer configurations display chemotactic and antichemotactic properties, with their behavior determined by the activity gradient strength. A coarsely detailed approach helps to generate an effective potential, used in our analysis to create a phase diagram. This diagram classifies dimer configurations based on their tactic behavior and also indicates how some dimers can maintain direction and achieve greater persistence in motion. This study provides valuable insights into the design of autonomous, responsive colloidal systems that can navigate according to varying activity levels in their environment.

The minimum strong shortest path cover with k-hops in a graph G is the smallest number of sets needed among all k-hops strong shortest path covers, where we also examine 2-hops covers for certain graphs and show the general k-hops cover problem is NP-complete.

The impact of infrared renormalons in the color dipole gluon distribution's variance is being quantified, and calculations demonstrate how non-linear small-x saturation impacts shift the Borel plane's IR pole from its initial position of $2/\beta_2$ to $1/\beta_1$, resulting in a change from the expected infrared uncertainty to one that better aligns with small-x saturation dynamics.

As the number of frogs per site grows, the frog model's behavior shifts from transient to recurrent on a d-ary rooted tree. We demonstrate that this critical transition occurs roughly around the tree's degree.

Researchers are focusing on extremely thin alloys made of rare earth and transition metals, with controlled composition and unique magnetic properties, to create advanced photonic applications that operate rapidly. Despite the potential, it is very difficult to achieve small scale dimensions, which are essential for scaling down devices, while maintaining the necessary functionality and maintaining the unique magnetic properties. This study demonstrates a breakthrough by integrating minute amounts of ferrimagnetic alloys within a gold nanoarray to create a highly complex crystal that reacts differently to light and controlled magnetic fields, resulting in clear and adjustable features in the spectral patterns. This discovery enables the development of precise light-sensing tools and provides a foundation for innovative technology that could manipulate magnetic properties with light in rare earth and transition metal alloys.

Knowledge distillation is a successful method for accelerating deep neural networks by training a compact model to mimic the behavior of a high-capacity network. Traditionally, this relies on having access to the original network's training data and parameters, which isn't always feasible due to storage or privacy constraints in real-world applications. This study introduces decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, allowing a model to be trained without access to the original network by distilling data and transferring both knowledge and pre-trained features from a reference model. It further introduces zero-shot black-box knowledge distillation, enabling a model to be trained based on interaction with the original network and distillation from the reference model, without requiring access to either. Two approaches, including a method transferring pre-trained features, are proposed, though the success depends on the reference model's similarity to the original network. Successful experiments demonstrate significant reduction in sample complexity and computational costs, showing at least five times fewer queries are needed compared to standard zero-shot learning, with similar accuracy results.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (4.3±0.5±0.3±0.3±0.6) ×10^-4, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (2.8±1.0±0.3±0.2±0.4) ×10^-4, with the given uncertainties stemming from various sources.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is generally a challenging task. Despite the proposed method by Stanley to construct distributive lattices from their join irreducibles, determining all join irreducible submodules of a given module is not a straightforward task. However, for modules that have no module composition multiplicities, we present an alternative approach based on the composition factors, drawing on the information about submodules and their lattices. Given input submodules that encompass all factors and are readily lattice-structure-known, we can reconstruct the lattice of submodules of the given module. The process is particularly demonstrated using specific modules associated with a family of Lie superalgebras, specifically for modules $M(\gl_n)$, for the $\osp(3,2)$, showing that their lattice structure matches that of extended free distributive lattices of rank 2, for $n\leq 3$.

A strong geodetic subset of a graph~$G$ comprises a selection of vertices~$S$, which allows for the coverage of the remaining vertices in~$G$, by establishing unique shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in~$S$. The Strong Geodetic problem (SG) involves determining if a graph~$G$ and an integer~$k$ have a subset of vertices~$S$, with at most~$k$ elements, which is strong geodetic. This problem has been proven to be NP-hard for all graphs. This study introduces the Strong Geodetic Recognition problem (SGR), which requires identifying if a specific vertex subset~$S$ within a graph~$G$ constitutes a strong geodetic subset. SGR is found to be NP-complete. Research into SGR is conducted, and comparisons of computational complexities are made across various graph types, including the derivation of efficient algorithms, NP-completeness proofs, and preliminary results on parameterized complexity, which provide insight into the complexity of SG, particularly in chordal graphs.

The ultimate goal of imitation learning is to develop efficient policies using nearly optimal expert examples. Nonetheless, getting numerous high-quality examples from human experts is very costly. On the other hand, getting vast amounts of low-quality or irrelevant paths from existing suboptimal policies is significantly cheaper. Nonetheless, the quality of these paths is very poor and thus not very helpful. In this project, we are looking at an imitation learning setting in which we have limited access to excellent expert trajectories but can access vast amounts of low-quality trajectories from suboptimal policies. Our objective is to find an algorithm that uses these two types of trajectories to derive a high-performing policy.
